en: to approach; to draw near; to loom

examples.ko: 시험이 코앞에 닥쳐오니까 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: The exam is right around the corner, so I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 태풍이 닥쳐온다는 뉴스를 보고 집에 일찍 갔어요.
examples.en: I saw the news that a typhoon was approaching and went home early.

examples.ko: 어려운 일이 닥쳐와도 포기하지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: I won't give up even when hard times come.

examples.ko: 이제 곧 마감이 닥쳐오는데 아직 반도 못 했어요.
examples.en: The deadline is almost here and I haven't even finished half.

examples.ko: 갑자기 닥쳐온 불행 앞에서 가족이 서로 힘이 되어 주었어요.
examples.en: Facing the misfortune that suddenly struck, the family supported each other.

examples.ko: 위기가 닥쳐왔지만 팀원들이 끝까지 힘을 냈어요.
examples.en: A crisis came, but the team members kept up their strength to the end.

explain: '다가오다'는 그냥 가까워지는 것이고, '닥쳐오다'는 시험, 위기, 태풍, 불행처럼 반갑지 않은 일이 바짝 가까워질 때 써요. 주어는 사람보다 일이나 상황인 경우가 많아요. '닥쳐오아'가 아니라 '닥쳐와요'로 줄여요.

phrases.en: The exam is closing in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '닥쳐오다'의 해요체로, '닥쳐오아요'가 아니라 이렇게 줄여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form of '닥쳐오다', contracted this way rather than '닥쳐오아요'.

phrases.en: We overcame the crisis that came upon us together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 관형사형으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: A past modifier form that describes the noun after it.
phrases.en_equiv: the crisis that came upon us

phrases.en: Winter is approaching.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그냥 가까워질 때 쓰고, '닥쳐오다'처럼 반갑지 않은 느낌은 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Simply means getting closer, without the unwelcome feeling of '닥쳐오다'.

explain_en: Threatening events like typhoons or crises draw near. '다가오다' just means getting closer, while '닥쳐오다' is for unwelcome things like exams, crises, typhoons or misfortune closing in. The subject is usually an event or situation rather than a person. The polite form is '닥쳐와요', not '닥쳐오아요'.

t90.ax: I won't give up even when hard times come.

en: to deny; to refuse to admit

examples.en: He denies the rumor.
The government denied responsibility.
You cannot deny the fact.
It looked strange that he denied it to the end.
He denied his mistake and got angry.
The company denied it, so the article was corrected.

explain: '아니라고 하다'와 비슷하지만 '부인하다'는 사실이나 혐의를 공식적으로 인정하지 않을 때 써요. 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 같은 소리의 '부인(아내)'과 헷갈리지 않게 문장 속 쓰임을 보세요.

phrases.example: 그 사실은 아무도 부인할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: No one can deny that fact.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분명한 사실이라서 아니라고 할 수 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is such a clear fact that it can't be denied.

phrases.en: He denied the charges.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often heard in the news.

phrases.example: 그는 자기가 한 일이 아니라고 해요.
phrases.en: He says he didn't do it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부인하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 부인하다 and good for everyday talk.

explain_en: Active: a person denies a fact or accusation about themselves. Similar to saying 'it is not so', but this verb is for officially refusing to admit a fact or accusation, and it is common in the news. Do not confuse it with a same-sounding noun that means wife or married woman.

dis.h: deny an accusation or a fact

p.n: 부정하다 sounds like rejecting the truth itself, not just denying a charge.

examples.ko: 불이 나자 동네 사람들이 모여 불구경을 했어요.
examples.en: When a fire broke out, the neighbors gathered to watch it.
I heard that watching a fire used to be a big spectacle in the old days.
Everyone stopped to watch the fire, so the road was very congested.

examples.ko: 안전한 곳에서 불구경하지 말고 신고부터 하세요.
examples.en: Do not just watch the fire from a safe place; report it first.

examples.ko: 남의 일을 불구경하듯 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You should not look at other people's problems like a bystander.

examples.ko: 불구경 나온 사람들 때문에 소방차가 지나가기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: The fire truck had trouble getting through because of the people who came out to watch.

explain: 실제로 불이 난 곳을 구경하는 일이지만, '불구경하듯'처럼 남의 일을 가만히 보기만 하는 태도를 말할 때도 써요. 실제 화재에서는 구경보다 신고와 대피가 먼저예요.

phrases.example: 회사가 어려운데 다들 강 건너 불구경하듯 해요.
phrases.en: The company is in trouble, but everyone acts as if it has nothing to do with them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기와 상관없는 일이라며 걱정 없이 지켜보기만 하는 태도를 말해요. 비판하거나 서운할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes watching passively, as if a problem has nothing to do with you. People use it when criticizing or feeling hurt by such an attitude.

explain_en: It literally means watching a fire, but '불구경하듯' is also used for watching someone else's problem passively. In a real fire, reporting it and evacuating come before watching.

examples.en: I went on a mountain hike with friends on the weekend.
It rained during the hike, so we came down.
This hike takes about three hours.
Gloves are a must for winter hikes.
I checked the hiking course in advance.
My father goes to a hiking club every month.

explain: '등산'과 거의 같지만 '산행'은 산길을 걷는 일정 전체의 느낌이 있어서 '산행 코스', '산행 모임'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '등산'이 더 흔하고, 산악회 안내문이나 후기에서 '산행'이 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 이번 산행 코스는 세 시간쯤 걸려요.
phrases.en: This hiking course takes about three hours.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걷는 길 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the whole route you walk.

phrases.en: I sometimes go hiking in autumn.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산행하다'보다 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out version of '산행하다'.

phrases.en: I met a new friend at the hiking club.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 산에 가는 모임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A group that goes to the mountains together.

explain_en: Sino-Korean, common in speech and writing; going up a mountain, often as a hobby. Nearly the same as '등산', but '산행' feels like the whole trek along mountain paths, so you get '산행 코스' and '산행 모임'. '등산' is more common in daily talk; '산행' shows up in hiking-club notices and trip reports.

t90.ax: This hike takes about three hours.

en: to wish; to hope; to desire

examples.en: I hope everyone stays healthy.
He always wished for his family to be happy.
I wrote a piece wishing for peace in the new year.
The thing I had hoped for finally came true.
We said goodbye wishing each other success.
If you wish earnestly, a way will open.

explain: '바라다'와 뜻은 가깝지만 '소망하다'는 더 간절하고 진지한 느낌이라 인사말, 편지, 기도, 글에서 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '바라요', '빌어요'가 더 자연스러워요. 같은 뜻의 명사는 '소망'이고 '소원'과 거의 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: I hope everyone stays healthy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 가깝지만 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요. '소망하다'는 더 간절하고 글에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning but more natural in daily talk, while 소망하다 is more earnest and suits writing.

phrases.en: I bought the house I had long hoped for.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-던'을 붙이면 오래전부터 바라 온 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-던' refers to something hoped for over a long time.

phrases.en: He achieved his wish and became a doctor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '소망'과 함께 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical collocation with the noun 소망.

explain_en: Personal hope for something good; mild, written or spoken. Close to '바라다' (to hope), but 소망하다 feels more earnest and serious, so it appears in greetings, letters, prayers, and writing. In daily talk, '바라요' or '빌어요' sound more natural. The noun '소망' is used almost like '소원' (a wish).

examples.en: The court judged this case fairly.
Citizens judge politicians through elections.
It is hard for one person to judge another.

examples.ko: 신이 모든 사람을 심판한다고 믿는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people believe God judges everyone.
They asked for the wrongdoer to be judged.

examples.ko: 먼저 사정을 듣고 나서 심판해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to hear the circumstances first and then judge.

explain: 경기에서 심판을 볼 때는 '심판을 보다'라고 해요. '심판하다'는 잘잘못을 가려 판정을 내린다는 무거운 느낌이라 재판이나 선거 이야기에 어울려요. '판단하다', '평가하다'보다 훨씬 강하게 들려요.

phrases.en: That person was judged in court.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심판을 받는 쪽에서 말해요. 재판이나 투표처럼 무거운 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is from the side of the one being judged. Use it for heavy matters like trials and votes.

phrases.en: The judge sorted out who was right and who was wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 맞고 틀렸는지 정한다는 뜻이에요. '심판하다'를 풀어 쓴 말로 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means deciding who was right or wrong. It is like an explanation of '심판하다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to decide who is at fault

phrases.en: I refereed a soccer game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기에서 규칙을 지키는지 보는 일이에요. 무거운 재판의 '심판'과는 느낌이 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means refereeing a game. It feels different from the heavy 'judgment' of a trial.

explain_en: Act as judge in a game or on a person. For refereeing a game, say '심판을 보다'. '심판하다' feels heavy, like weighing right and wrong and passing judgment, so it fits talk about trials and elections. It sounds much stronger than '판단하다' or '평가하다'.

t90.ax: The court judged this case fairly.

en: to intend; to aim; to design

examples.en: I didn't mean to say that.
Let's think about what the author intended.
I didn't do it on purpose.
It didn't go the way I intended.

examples.ko: 광고를 만든 사람은 사람들이 웃도록 의도했어요.
examples.en: The person who made the ad intended people to laugh.

examples.ko: 그 일을 처음부터 의도했다면 더 큰 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: If you intended that from the start, it becomes a bigger problem.

explain: '의도'는 마음속의 목적이에요. 사과할 때 '의도하지 않았어요'라고 말할 수 있어요. '일부러'는 더 일상적인 말이에요.

phrases.en: I didn't intend it that way. I'm sorry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실수했을 때 나쁜 뜻이 없었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you made a mistake and want to say you meant no harm.

phrases.example: 모든 일이 의도한 대로 잘 됐어요.
phrases.en: Everything went well as I intended.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대로'와 함께 계획한 것과 같다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '대로', it means things turned out as planned.

phrases.example: 저는 일부러 그 말을 한 게 아니에요.
phrases.en: I didn't say that on purpose.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의도하다'보다 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday word than '의도하다'.

explain_en: '의도' is the purpose in your mind. When apologizing you can say '의도하지 않았어요'. '일부러' is the more casual everyday word.

examples.en: The soldiers kept advancing forward.
The car parked by repeatedly moving forward and backward.
Even a small step forward matters.

examples.ko: 팀은 결승 진출로 한 걸음 전진했어요.
examples.en: The team took a step forward by reaching the final.
The robot moves when you press the forward button.
The teacher told us not to stop moving forward.

explain: 전진은 앞으로 나아가는 것이에요. 반대말은 '후진'이고, 자동차 기어에서도 '전진'과 '후진'으로 나눠요. 일이 앞으로 발전할 때도 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 이번 시험으로 꿈에 한 걸음 전진했어요.
phrases.en: With this exam, I took one step closer to my dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작지만 앞으로 나아간 발전을 말할 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to describe a small step forward.

phrases.en: To start the car, switch to the forward gear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차에서 앞으로 가는 기어를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the gear that moves a car forward.

phrases.en: The captain gave the order to advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대나 팀에게 앞으로 가라고 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An order telling a group to move ahead.

explain_en: 전진 is moving forward. The opposite is '후진', and car gears are also split into 전진 and 후진. It can also be used figuratively for making progress.

t90.ax: Even a small step forward matters.

examples.en: A new problem was raised.
Various opinions are raised in the meeting.
I'll answer the questions being raised one by one.
When a problem is raised, we check right away.
Let's solve the problems already raised first.
I explained every time a doubt was raised.

explain: 문제, 의혹, 질문 같은 말이 나올 때만 써요. 앞에 보통 '문제가', '의견이'가 와요. 사람이 꺼내면 '제기하다'예요.

phrases.en: A safety problem was raised at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제기되다' 앞에 가장 자주 오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase that goes with '제기되다'.

phrases.en: Doubts were raised about that result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿기 어려운 일에 질문이 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when questions come up about something hard to believe.

phrases.example: 이 문제는 오래전부터 계속 제기되고 있어요.
phrases.en: This issue has been raised for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 계속 나오고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when an issue keeps coming up.

explain_en: Use it only when issues, doubts, or questions come up. It is usually preceded by '문제가' or '의견이'. When a person raises it, use '제기하다'.

examples.en: The director cast a new actor.

examples.ko: 제작사는 유명한 가수를 캐스팅하고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The production company wants to cast a famous singer.

examples.ko: 그 역할에 누구를 캐스팅할지 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: We are thinking about who to cast in that role.
I watched a video of the casting process.
A news story said they had cast the lead.

examples.ko: 어린이 역은 오디션 없이 캐스팅하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to cast the children's roles without an audition.

explain: '배우를 캐스팅하다'처럼 고르는 쪽이 주어예요. 뽑힌 배우 쪽에서는 '캐스팅되다'를 써요. 길에서 배우나 모델 후보를 찾는 것은 '길거리 캐스팅'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That model debuted through street casting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 후보를 찾는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to finding candidates on the street.

phrases.example: 감독님은 그 배우를 캐스팅하고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: The director wants to cast that actor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뽑는 쪽의 바람을 다른 사람이 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the wish of the person choosing, from a third-person view.

phrases.en: Famous actors are hard to cast.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 어렵다'로 어려움을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -기 어렵다 to say something is hard.

explain_en: The one choosing is the subject, as in '배우를 캐스팅하다' (cast an actor). From the chosen actor's side, '캐스팅되다' is used. Finding acting or modeling talent on the street is called '길거리 캐스팅' (street casting).

t90.ax: The director cast a new actor.

en: to put one on top of another; to stack

examples.en: I stacked the bowls one by one and put them in the cupboard.

examples.ko: 의자를 포개 놓으면 자리를 덜 차지해요.
examples.en: If you stack the chairs, they take up less space.

examples.ko: 아이가 손을 내 손 위에 포갰어요.
examples.en: The child laid her hand on top of mine.
If you stack paper cups too high, they fall over.
If you stack the T-shirts, the closet looks neat.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 다리를 포개고 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: The two of them are sitting with their legs crossed one over the other.

explain: 같은 모양의 물건을 위에 겹쳐서 놓을 때 써요. 그릇, 의자, 손처럼 서로 맞게 겹치는 느낌이 있어요. 높이 쌓을 때는 '쌓다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 종이를 접어 겹칠 때는 '겹치다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I stacked the plates one on top of another.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겹쳐서 둔 결과 상태까지 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that things are placed on top of each other and left that way.

phrases.en: The boxes are stacked together, so they're hard to take out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 겹쳐진 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes things that are already stacked.

phrases.example: 아이가 무릎 위에 두 손을 포개고 앉았어요.
phrases.en: The child sat with both hands folded on their lap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손이나 다리를 겹칠 때도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also commonly used for laying hands one over the other.
phrases.en_equiv: to fold hands one over the other

explain_en: Use it for laying items of the same shape on top of one another, like bowls, chairs or hands, so they fit together. For tall piles, '쌓다' is more common, and for overlapping paper, '겹치다' sounds natural.

examples.en: There are bodyguards beside the president.
The singer arrived at the airport with bodyguards.
The bodyguard made the fans step back.

examples.ko: 형은 경호원이 되려고 운동을 열심히 해요.
examples.en: My brother exercises hard to become a bodyguard.
A security guard checked the bags at the event entrance.
A bodyguard's eyes are always scanning the surroundings.

explain: 경호원은 중요한 사람을 위험에서 지키는 사람이에요. 건물이나 가게를 지키는 사람은 '경비원', '보안 요원'이라고 해서 달라요. 정치인이나 연예인 같은 특정한 사람 옆에서 지킬 때 경호원이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That actor goes around with a bodyguard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경호원과 같은 뜻의 외래어예요. 대화나 영화 이야기에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A loanword with the same meaning as 경호원, used casually in conversation or when talking about movies.

phrases.en: The bodyguards protect the president.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경호원이 하는 일을 동사로 말할 때 써요. 중요한 사람을 지킨다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for what a bodyguard does: protecting an important person.

phrases.en: The president is always under protection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지켜 주는 사람이 아니라 보호받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the viewpoint of the person being protected, not the one protecting.

explain_en: Guards a VIP or celebrity closely, as at a concert. A gyeonghowon protects an important person from danger. Someone guarding a building or shop is a 경비원 or 보안 요원, which is different. 경호원 is used for those who stay beside specific people such as politicians or celebrities.

examples.en: I was a bridesmaid at my friend's wedding.
My younger sister became my older sister's bridesmaid.
We picked the bridesmaid dresses together.

examples.ko: 신부 들러리들이 꽃을 들고 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The bride's attendants stood holding flowers.

examples.ko: 들러리는 보통 신부와 친한 친구가 맡아요.
examples.en: A bridesmaid is usually a close friend of the bride.
I gave a thank-you gift to the bridesmaid.

explain: 결혼식에서 신부나 신랑 곁에 서는 사람을 말하고, 동사는 '서다'를 써서 '들러리를 서다'라고 해요. 누구의 들러리인지 앞에 붙여서 '신부 들러리'처럼 써요. 비유로도 많이 써서 아래 표현을 같이 보세요.

phrases.example: 이번 대회는 우승자가 정해져 있어서 저는 들러리만 선 것 같아요.
phrases.en: just be there to make someone else look good
phrases.nuance_ko: 중심이 아니라 다른 사람을 돋보이게 해 주는 역할만 한다는 비유예요. 조금 서운한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for playing only a supporting role while someone else is the star. It carries a slightly resentful feeling.

explain_en: It refers to someone standing beside the bride or groom at a wedding, with the verb '서다': '들러리를 서다'. Put the person in front, as in '신부 들러리'. It is also used figuratively; see the expression below.

examples.en: I can see the grains of rice one by one.
Pomegranate seeds are tasty even if you chew them whole.
I put the corn kernels on a plate.

examples.ko: 이 비누는 작은 알갱이로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This soap is made of tiny granules.

examples.ko: 소금 알갱이가 굵어서 잘 녹지 않아요.
examples.en: The salt grains are coarse, so they don't dissolve easily.
Grains of sand got inside my shoe.

explain: 쌀, 소금, 모래, 곡식처럼 가루보다는 크고 덩어리보다는 작은 낱개에 잘 어울려요. 세는 말은 '쌀 한 알'처럼 '알'을 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The salt grains are big, so they dissolve slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소금처럼 작은 낱개를 하나하나 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when seeing small individual pieces like salt grains.

phrases.en: Grains of sand got inside my shoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모래의 작은 낱개를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the small individual pieces of sand.

phrases.en: The grains of this rice are large.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낱개의 크기를 설명할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression for describing the size of individual grains.

explain_en: Any small round bit, like sugar or sand. It suits things like rice, salt, sand and grain: bigger than powder, smaller than lumps. The counter 알 is often used, as in '쌀 한 알'.

t90.ax: I put the corn kernels on a plate.

examples.en: It's really dangerous to climb onto the railroad tracks.
The train passed slowly along the tracks.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 철로 옆이라서 기차 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: My house is next to the tracks, so I hear trains.
Construction to lay new tracks has begun.
A lot of snow fell, so the tracks froze.

examples.ko: 옛날 철로를 산책길로 바꾼 곳이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a place where old tracks were turned into a walking path.

explain: 철로는 기차가 다니는 길, 즉 레일이 놓인 길이에요. 비슷한 '선로'는 철도 용어로 더 많이 쓰고, 철로는 일상에서 길로서의 느낌이 강해요. 둘을 거의 같은 뜻으로 써도 괜찮아요.

phrases.en: Be careful when you cross the railroad tracks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기찻길을 가로질러 지나갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when crossing over the railway.

phrases.en: A new railroad was laid at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 길이 만들어졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a new track has been built.

phrases.en: The train is late because of track work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 철로와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 철도 일에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 철로, but more common in railway work.

explain_en: The track as a route, somewhat written (철로 위) 철로 is the path on which trains run, meaning the road where rails are laid. The similar 선로 is used more as a railway term, while 철로 feels more like a road in everyday talk. You can use the two with almost the same meaning.

t90.ax: A lot of snow fell, so the tracks froze.
